sections.title: SRE Incident Lifecycle & Service Level Objectives
sections.content:
### Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) Outage Response

When high-severity incidents (SEV-1 / P1) occur, structured operational triage is critical to maintaining high availability (>99.99% uptime):

```text
Incident Timeline:
[Detection / Pager Alert] ──> [Triage & Containment] ──> [Root Cause Mitigation] ──> [Post-Mortem & Blameless RCA]
```

#### Core SRE Metrics (The 4 Golden Signals):
1. **Latency**: Time taken to service a request (differentiating between successful and error latency).
2. **Traffic**: Demand placed on the system (HTTP requests/sec or IOPS).
3. **Errors**: The rate of requests that fail (HTTP 5xx, failed DB queries, broken network connections).
4. **Saturation**: How 'full' the service is (CPU, RAM, disk I/O, socket descriptors).

sections.title: Diagnosing CrashLoopBackOff & OOMKilled
sections.content:
### Kubernetes Failure Modes

When a container fails to start or continuously terminates, Kubernetes labels it with specific exit statuses:

| State | Primary Root Cause | First Diagnostic Step |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **CrashLoopBackOff (Exit 1)** | Application error, missing env var, syntax crash | `kubectl logs <pod> --previous` |
| **OOMKilled (Exit 137)** | Container exceeded memory `limits` (Linux OOM killer) | `kubectl describe pod <pod>` (Look for `Last State: Terminated, Exit Code: 137`) |
| **ImagePullBackOff** | Registry authentication failure or non-existent image tag | Check image name and Docker secret credentials |
| **CreateContainerConfigError** | Missing ConfigMap key or Secret reference | `kubectl get configmap,secret` |

sections.title: CoreDNS Failures & The ndots:5 Bottleneck
sections.content:
### Debugging DNS Outages in Cloud Workloads

By default, `/etc/resolv.conf` in Kubernetes pods sets `options ndots:5`. For external domains like `api.stripe.com`, Linux performs up to 4 sequential DNS queries inside cluster search domains (`default.svc.cluster.local`, `svc.cluster.local`, `cluster.local`) before querying the public root.

```text
Client Request: api.stripe.com
1. api.stripe.com.default.svc.cluster.local  -> NXDOMAIN (Latency penalty)
2. api.stripe.com.svc.cluster.local          -> NXDOMAIN
3. api.stripe.com.cluster.local              -> NXDOMAIN
4. api.stripe.com                            -> SUCCESS (Resolved)
```

**Fix**: Append a trailing dot (`api.stripe.com.`) in application configs to bypass search domain penalties and reduce DNS lookups by 75%.

quiz.question: What is the primary indicator that a Kubernetes Pod was killed by the Linux Out-of-Memory (OOM) killer?
options: Exit code 137 in container Last State
Pod state set to Evicted due to disk pressure
quiz.explanation: Exit code 137 corresponds to 128 + 9 (SIGKILL), indicating the Linux kernel OOM killer forcibly terminated the process for violating memory limits.

quiz.question: Why does adding a trailing dot (e.g. `api.example.com.`) improve external DNS query latency in Kubernetes pods?
options: It signals to the resolver that the domain is Fully Qualified (FQDN), bypassing ndots search domain expansions
It switches the query protocol from UDP to TCP automatically
It forces CoreDNS to cache responses indefinitely
It encrypts DNS queries with DNS-over-HTTPS
quiz.explanation: A trailing dot indicates a Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN), which skips search domain expansions defined in ndots:5.
